historical_cutoff.rule: Completion of the final scheduled game of Week 7
historical_cutoff.cutoff: Immediately after actual completion of the final scheduled Week 7 game; Stage 1 must verify completion and exclude all Week 8 games.

records.context_summary: Starting QB; back-to-back 300-yard, zero-INT starts (305 vs ATL, 308 vs NE), 71% completion, 105.6 rating. Bears offense 3rd in yards and 1st in rushing. Seattle pass defense 1st (144.4 allowed/game), has not allowed >176 passing yards and has 12 takeaways. Recent hamstring absence resolved; no current status. Multiple productive receiving options (Burden, Loveland, Odunze) create target distribution. Run-heavy team identity may reduce attempts. Weather negligible. Implication: recent QB form strong, but severe opponent suppression makes passing-yard ceiling uncertain.

Confirmed starter, 100% Week 7 snaps; 1,290 pass yards, 8 TD, 8 INT, 62.1% completion, 80.5 rating. Intercepted in each of last five games. Chicago adds Jeffery Simmons and returns Montez Sweat/T.J. Edwards. Seattle LT Charles Cross OUT; Josh Jones starts, Quenton Nelson joins at LG, Grey Zabel shifts to RG; Anthony Bradford questionable. Drew Lock questionable but Darnold starts. JSN commands 36.3% targets; Shaheed OUT (14% share) may consolidate targets. Weather negligible. Implication: Chicago pass defense not top-ranked by yardage, but turnover form and OL adjustment are material negatives.

Lead Bears RB; 476 rush yards and 7 TD on 116 carries; 62% season snap share, 86% Week 7. Chicago ranks 1st rushing (154.3/game). Monangai OUT (thumb/toe), Swift no injury, increasing opportunity; Roschon Johnson remains. Seattle has not allowed a 100-yard rusher in 36 straight games incl postseason; strong front. Bears may control possession with run game. Weather neutral. Implication: volume is supportive, but Seattle's remarkable run-defense streak caps confidence in high yardage.

Seattle RB had 24 carries (58.5% of team), 25 opportunities and 48% snaps Week 7; season snap share ~41%. That workload preceded Charbonnet's return: Charbonnet confirmed playing after ACL recovery; Jadarian Price returned to full practice/available, and George Holani remains. Chicago run defense allows 87.6 rush yards/game (3rd per matchup data). Seattle OL adjusting with Cross OUT, Josh Jones at LT, Nelson at LG, Zabel at RG; Bradford questionable. Implication: do not project Week 7 carry share forward; major workload uncertainty against strong run defense.

Starting WR, 85% snap share; 38 targets, 24 catches, 381 yards, 17% season target share; recent 3-week share remains 17%. Seattle pass defense 1st, 144.4 yards allowed/game, Devon Witherspoon anchors secondary. No injury status. Caleb returned with two 300-yard games. Chicago ranks 1st rushing and has several viable targets: Burden 21%, Loveland 18.8%, Raymond 13.8%. Weather neutral. Implication: stable role but difficult coverage and target competition.

85% snap share; 24 catches on 38 targets, 17% season and recent 3-week target share. Seattle allows fewest pass yards and has not allowed >176 pass yards. No injury status; Williams in strong recent form. Bears balanced offense with strong run game; target tree shared with Burden (21%), Loveland (18.8%), Raymond (13.8%). Weather neutral. Implication: role supports involvement, but pass-defense strength and competing targets create uncertainty.

Starting Bears WR, 60% season snap share; 47 targets, 35 catches, 491 yards, 21% season share. Recent 2 games: 95 yards on 8 catches vs ATL; 130 yards on 4 catches vs NE. Last-three-week share down to 17% vs 21% season. Seattle #1 pass defense; Bears preview highlights matchup vs Devon Witherspoon (3-time Pro Bowler). No injury; Williams returned. Burden's YAC/screens offer explosive-play path, but Odunze/Loveland compete. Weather neutral. Implication: explosive recent output and strong season share offset by Witherspoon and recent share decline.

60% snap share; 47 targets/35 catches; 21% season target share but 17% last three weeks. 12 catches in last two games. Seattle pass defense ranks 1st; Witherspoon matchup is difficult. No injury; Williams returned. Short-area screens/YAC support catch opportunity; Odunze and Loveland are target competitors. Weather neutral. Implication: recent catches encouraging, but snap share and matchup prevent strong confidence.

Bears WR, 61% season snap share; 31 targets, 26 catches, 244 yards; 13.8% season share but about 8% over last three weeks (down 7 points vs earlier weeks). Seattle pass defense #1. No injury; Williams form improves team outlook, not Raymond's allocation. Burden, Odunze, Loveland all command stronger roles. Weather neutral. Implication: season totals overstate current opportunity; declining targets and elite defense weaken yardage path.

61% season snap share; 26 catches on 31 targets; 13.8% season target share but about 8% recent share. Seattle pass defense #1. No injury. Williams is healthy and playing well, but target allocation favours Burden, Odunze and Loveland. Raymond's secondary slot role is volume-dependent. Weather neutral. Implication: low line may look attractive on season results, but recent target decline is adverse.

Seattle WR1, 83% season snap share; leads NFL with 867 receiving yards and 8 TD; 58 catches on 78 targets, 36.3% share. Week 7: 12 targets, 44.4% team share, 77% snaps. Chicago pass defense allows 225.9 yards/game in current context data; Bears add Simmons and return Sweat. JSN full practice; Shaheed OUT (14% target share). Darnold has 8 INT and five straight games with an INT; Cross OUT, Josh Jones LT, Nelson at LG, Zabel RG. Weather neutral. Implication: elite target concentration and Shaheed absence support opportunity; QB/OL risk offsets.

83% season snap share; 58 catches on 78 targets, 36.3% share; 12 targets and 44.4% team share Week 7. Shaheed OUT may consolidate targets. Chicago's pass defense allows 225.9 yards/game, but Simmons/Sweat strengthen pass rush. JSN full practice. Darnold turnover streak and Cross OUT/line reshuffle are risks. Weather neutral. Implication: strongest receiving-role security in game; QB/protection are main caveats.

Seattle WR with 68% season snap share; 27 targets and 12.6% season share. Week 7 only 2 targets (7.4% team share) and 65% snaps. Shaheed OUT could free targets. No injury status. Darnold has INT in five straight; Cross OUT and Seattle OL changing. JSN dominates target tree; Barner has 13.5% share, Tory Horton also available. Weather neutral. Implication: possible extra opportunity from Shaheed absence, but recent usage and target competition make catch volume uncertain.

Bears primary TE, 86% season snap share; 42 targets (18.8% share), 26 catches, 244 yards. Recent share up to 23% last three weeks; 12 targets Week 7. Cole Kmet season-ending injury consolidates TE role. NFL Week 8 report lists Loveland full participation/no game status after earlier neck limitation. Williams returned to strong form. Seattle pass defense #1 is major counterweight. Burden/Odunze compete, but Loveland's recent share has risen. Weather neutral. Implication: secure role and rising targets support catches, with difficult opponent as main concern.

Seattle starting TE, 88% season snap share; 29 targets, 13.5% season share. Week 7: 5 targets (18.5% team share), 80% snaps. No injury status; Shaheed OUT may redistribute targets. Darnold turnover streak and Cross OUT/OL reshuffle are concerns; Bradford questionable. JSN dominates, Kupp and Horton also available. Weather neutral. Implication: stable route participation and recent target uptick help, but secondary share and QB/protection risks temper confidence.

tier_methodology.note: The Master Prompt prohibits Tier 3 in Low Variance but does not separately define the tier cutoffs. To operationalize R28 without introducing an external standard, the tier labels are mapped directly to the three HR bands explicitly specified in R23. This interpretation is disclosed, not represented as a separately stated definition in the prompt.
